test_title: PYST 34: SSC CGL 2024 - Quantitative Aptitude (Held On: 26 Sept, 2024 Shift 1)
subject: maths
question: ΔABC is a right-angled triangle with ∠ABC = 90°. If m(AB) = 28 cm, and m(BC) = 96 cm, find the area (in cm²) of the circumcircle of ΔABC. (Use π = 3.14.)
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a right-angled triangle, the circumcenter always lies at the midpoint of the hypotenuse.

This means the hypotenuse acts as the diameter of the circumcircle.

Using the standard Pythagorean triplet (7, 24, 25), we multiply by 4 to get sides (28, 96, 100), making hypotenuse AC = 100 cm.

Circumradius (R) = 100 ÷ 2 = 50 cm.

Area of circumcircle = π × R² = 3.14 × 2500 = 7850 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 7850 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

m(AB) = 28 cm

m(BC) = 96 cm

∠ABC = 90°

π = 3.14

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/238eef97d4428dba6e115697d2afed3bf9b23841fb1a7c89daeeab57e4a7a6ec.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Hypotenuse = √(Perpendicular² + Base²)

Circumradius (R) = Hypotenuse ÷ 2

Area of Circle = π × R²

**Calculations:**

⇒ In right-angled ΔABC, apply Pythagorean theorem to find hypotenuse AC:

⇒ AC = √(AB² + BC²)

⇒ AC = √(28² + 96²)

⇒ AC = √(784 + 9216)

⇒ AC = √10000 = 100 cm

⇒ The hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle forms the diameter of its circumcircle.

⇒ Circumradius (R) = AC ÷ 2

⇒ Circumradius (R) = 100 ÷ 2 = 50 cm

⇒ Area of Circumcircle = 3.14 × (50)²

⇒ Area = 3.14 × 2500

⇒ Area = 7850 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 7850 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Circumcenter of a Right-Angled Triangle

The circumcenter lies exactly at the midpoint of the hypotenuse, making the circumradius equal to half the hypotenuse (R = h ÷ 2).

Inradius of a Right-Angled Triangle

The radius of the inscribed circle can be calculated directly using the formula r = (Perpendicular + Base − Hypotenuse) ÷ 2.

Pythagorean Triplets

A set of three positive integers (a, b, c) that satisfy a² + b² = c². Common primitive triplets include (3, 4, 5), (5, 12, 13), and (7, 24, 25).
